purpose: Document the fairness issue in the B06-original vs B07-DYNAMIC-V2 comparison and the resolution implemented by B06-V2-FAIR.

inputs.rationale: Fixed mixed-type inputs designed for general Python programs
SAFEGUARD-3: v2 inputs independent from v1; list-only to match benchmark program signatures

fairness_issue.description: The comparison B06-original vs B07-DYNAMIC-V2 simultaneously varies two independent factors: (1) the input set used for execution and (2) the feature representation derived from those traces. This is a confounded comparison — any observed difference in AUROC cannot be attributed solely to the feature representation choice.

variable_1_inputs.confound: YES — different coverage of program behaviour; mixed types may cause more exceptions in list-sorting programs, inflating exception_rate similarity artificially

variable_2_features.b06_original: Flat trace features: call bigrams + coverage + ret type + exception rate
variable_2_features.b07_dynamic_v2: DynamicGenome: structured representation via SandboxRunner + TraceNormalizer
variable_2_features.confound: YES — this is the intended experimental variable

fairness_issue.impact: The +0.0264 AUROC gap (0.5310 - 0.5046) cannot be cleanly attributed to DynamicGenome vs flat features because the input protocol also changed. SAFEGUARD-5 in the Phase 0 audit explicitly required re-running B06 with v2 input protocol before claiming improvement.

b06_fair_v2_configuration.what_changed_from_b06_original: ONLY the input set. The input protocol was changed from 14 mixed-type v1 inputs to 8 list-only V2_CANONICAL_INPUTS imported directly from B07.
what_did_not_change: Feature representation (B06 flat trace: call bigrams, coverage, ret type, exception rate)
Threshold selection protocol (DEV split only, frozen for TEST)
AUROC computation (1 - similarity as CHANGED score)

why_fair.same_programs: Both B06-V2-FAIR and B07 evaluate on the same benchmark/datasets/pairs_dev.jsonl and pairs_test.jsonl.
why_fair.same_labels: Both use the semantic_relation field: EQUIVALENT=0, CHANGED=1.
why_fair.same_split: Both use DEV to select threshold, TEST to report final metrics. TEST threshold never inspected during selection.
why_fair.same_inputs: Both use V2_CANONICAL_INPUTS imported from b07_dynamic_v2.py — the import statement is the concrete guarantee of identity.
why_fair.only_difference: Feature representation: B06-V2-FAIR uses flat trace aggregates; B07 uses DynamicGenome. This is the single independent variable under test.
why_fair.conclusion: B06-V2-FAIR vs B07-DYNAMIC-V2 is a controlled comparison of feature representations under a fixed execution protocol.

expected_impact_of_input_change.hypothesis: Switching from mixed-type v1 inputs to list-only v2 inputs should IMPROVE B06's AUROC on this benchmark because the benchmark programs are predominantly list-processing algorithms. Mixed-type inputs (int, str) cause exceptions that contaminate the exception_rate feature with noise unrelated to algorithmic differences.
expected_impact_of_input_change.prediction: B06-V2-FAIR AUROC > B06-original AUROC (0.5046). Magnitude uncertain; likely small.
expected_impact_of_input_change.null_hypothesis: Input change has no effect on ranking quality; AUROC difference is within bootstrap CI overlap.
expected_impact_of_input_change.note: If B06-V2-FAIR AUROC is significantly higher than B06-original, the reported v1 B06 number is an underestimate of flat-feature capability caused by input mismatch, not algorithmic limitation.
